title: Chicken Liver Crostini with Sage
summary: Crisp baked crostini spread with a smooth, savoury chicken liver pâté seasoned with garlic, sage and anchovy, each crowned with a fresh sage leaf.

ingredients.item: chicken livers, trimmed of sinew and patted dry
fine sea salt or table salt
small fresh sage leaves, to garnish

steps.title: Crostini
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180 °C (160 °C fan). Brush the bread slices lightly with oil and bake for 10-12 minutes, until crisp with golden edges. Baking dries them right through, so they stay crunchy under the soft spread.

steps.title: Sear the livers
steps.text: Heat the 3 tbsp oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Lay the livers in a single layer and cook for 2-3 minutes a side, until well browned outside; dry livers in an uncrowded pan brown instead of stewing.

steps.title: Finish cooking
steps.text: Turn the heat down, add the garlic and chopped sage and cook for 1-2 minutes more, until the livers are no longer pink in the centre and read 74 °C. Lower heat lets the middle cook through without the garlic burning.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Scrape everything, including the pan oil, into a food processor with the anchovies, lemon juice, salt and pepper, and blend until smooth. Taste and adjust; the anchovies melt into the spread and add depth rather than a fishy taste.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Spread a heaped tablespoon of pâté on each crostino and press a sage leaf on top. Serve warm or at room temperature, when the flavour is fullest.

tips: Trim away any green patches on the livers, as they taste bitter.
If the pâté is too thick to blend, add 1-2 tsp warm water.
Bake the crostini a day ahead and keep them in an airtight tin.
safety: Undercooking is the mistake to avoid: chicken livers must reach 74 °C in the centre. Check the thickest one with a thermometer.
storage: Keep the pâté covered in the fridge for up to 2 days; bring it to room temperature before spreading. Crostini keep in an airtight tin for 3 days. Do not freeze the assembled crostini. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
